---
title: "Drainage-area contributions"
---

## Monthly water balance

Each drainage area generates a local contribution based on precipitation, evapotranspiration, snow and the drained area.

$$
Q^{contrib}_{i,m}
=
\frac{
A_i\,C
\left(
P_{i,m}-ET_{i,m}-r_m\Delta N_{i,m}
\right)
}{
1000\,S_m
}
$$

where:

- $Q^{contrib}_{i,m}$: flow contributed by area $i$ during month $m$, in $\mathrm{m^3\,s^{-1}}$;
- $A_i$: drainage area, in $\mathrm{m^2}$;
- $C$: runoff coefficient;
- $P_{i,m}$: monthly precipitation, in mm;
- $ET_{i,m}$: monthly actual evapotranspiration, in mm;
- $\Delta N_{i,m}$: monthly change in snow storage;
- $r_m$: conversion factor from snow to water equivalent;
- $S_m$: duration of the month, in seconds;
- the factor $1000$ converts millimetres to metres.

## Evapotranspiration

Monthly potential evapotranspiration is calculated from mean monthly temperature using the Thornthwaite method:

$$
PET_m =
16
\left(
\frac{10T_m}{I}
\right)^a
K_m
$$

where:

$$
I=\sum_{m=1}^{12}
\left(
\frac{T_m}{5}
\right)^{1.514}
$$

and:

$$
a =
6.75\times10^{-7}I^3
-
7.71\times10^{-5}I^2
+
1.792\times10^{-2}I
+
0.49239
$$

$K_m$ corrects the result for day length and the number of days in the month.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Interpretation

PET represents the evaporative demand of the atmosphere if sufficient water were available. It is not necessarily the amount of water actually evapotranspired by the basin.
:::

For each land use $u$, actual evapotranspiration is calculated using a formulation based on precipitation, PET and a vegetation coefficient^[Mas-Pla, J. et al. (2016). “Recursos hidrològics”. In [Tercer informe sobre el canvi climàtic a Catalunya](https://cads.gencat.cat/ca/publicacions/informes-sobre-el-canvi-climatic-a-catalunya/tercer-informe-sobre-el-canvi-climatic-a-catalunya-/index.html), pp. 161–188]:

$$
ET_{i,m}
=
\sum_u f_{i,u}
\,
P_{i,m}
\,
\frac{
1+w_u\frac{PET_{i,m}}{P_{i,m}}
}{
1+w_u\frac{PET_{i,m}}{P_{i,m}}
+\frac{P_{i,m}}{PET_{i,m}}
}
$$

where:

- $f_{i,u}$: proportion of land use $u$ within area $i$;
- $w_u$: evapotranspiration coefficient for the land use;
- $P_{i,m}$: monthly precipitation;
- $PET_{i,m}$: potential evapotranspiration.

### Coefficients by land use

| Land use | $w_u$ |
|---|---:|
| Water | 0 |
| Urban land and impervious surfaces | 0 |
| Forest and tree plantations | 1.75 |
| Natural grassland and pasture | 1.00 |
| Rainfed crops | 0.75 |
| Irrigated crops | 1.50 |

Higher values represent a greater capacity of vegetation to use the available water.

::: {.callout-warning}
The model represents the effect of land use on evapotranspiration in an aggregated manner. It does not explicitly simulate soil moisture, rooting or vegetation growth.
:::
